sections.What the paper proposes: The paper (Oil-Price Exposure as a Single-Factor Smart-Beta Strategy) proposes OILP is each security's slope coefficient b_i,oil from a time-series regression of its returns on monthly simple oil-price changes plus other risk controls, estimated on a training sample. A constrained long-short optimizer builds positive, neutral and negative OILP-target portfolios (maximizing exposure to historical residual returns subject to the OILP target, other factor targets, gross long/short allocations and name bounds); a timing signal s(t) picks positive if s(t) >= h, negative if s(t) <= -h, neutral otherwise as the signal, sorted by other, favoring the positive-OILP portfolio, conditional on higher contemporaneous or correctly forecast oil returns (no unconditional premium claimed). Rationale: Oil-price innovations affect firms differently through production costs, revenues, demand conditions and discount-rate channels; conditionally, higher oil returns favor positive oil exposure and lower oil returns favor negative exposure. No unconditional premium is claimed.
sections.What we implemented and changed: We adapted 7 fields and assumed 7. Adapted: sort_rule (paper sort 'other' is not a ranked-group sort; deciles with equal-count breakpoints); weighting (policy: equal weight everywhere); disfavored_group (policy: long-only, no short leg); universe_and_filters (policy: our 415-name S&P 500 survivor universe); sample_period (policy: our snapshot sample); timing_signal (the note's signal is built from realized future oil returns (an oracle); the engine tests the exposure sort only); oil_series (after the oil series ends, regressions use available paired observations until fewer than 24 remain; a skipped formation issues no new target, so existing holdings carry forward). Assumed: formation_window set to 36; favored_group set to highest group; expected_sign set to favored_group_higher; skip_window set to 0 months; price_floor set to none; min_history_days set to 756; min_formation_days set to 15. Portfolios were formed in 123 months with 36.6 names on average. The oil input ends in March 2024. The regression uses remaining paired observations; the last selected formation is 2025-03-31 and the last rebalance is 2025-04-01. Missing formations issue no new target: existing holdings carry forward and their subsequent returns remain in the evaluation.
sections.What the backtest found: Over the sample the strategy returned 15.80% a year net of costs, against 12.83% for the equal-weight universe and 13.45% for SPY. Its Sharpe ratio was 0.63 against 0.66 for the equal-weight universe, and its maximum drawdown was -48.8%. The alpha t-statistic was 1.40; it is reported, not used as a gate. Robustness across costs, sub-periods and ranked groups gave a rho of 0.92.
sections.What the simulation and economics found: Across the simulated paths, incremental fee income versus the equal-weight universe fund had a median present value of $4.4M, with a 5th to 95th percentile range of -$2.8M to $23.1M. The share of paths with positive NPV after research cost was 79.5%, and 48.9% once the historical excess return is removed. Break-even AUM is $303k; it is reported, not headlined.
sections.How reliable the interpretation was: Across 2 extraction runs the material fields agreed on average 75.0% of the time, and evidence was valid for 100.0% of material fields with 1 check-pass disagreements. Quote matching and extraction agreement do not establish independent correctness.
